meaning: Isistius, see genus; brasiliensis, Latin suffix -ensis denoting place: off the coast of Brazil, the type locality
description: A tiny, cigar-shaped, chocolate-brown shark with a short blunt snout, large green eyes and a dark collar around the throat; its belly glows with light-producing photophores. It rises toward the surface at night, latches on with suction-cup lips and cuts a round plug of flesh from tuna, whales and other larger animals with its saw-like lower teeth.
depth: Surface to about 3,700 m; deep by day, shallower at night
eats: Squid, crustaceans and small fish, plus plugs of flesh bitten from larger fish and marine mammals
